back: Checks each item in turn from the first until the item is found or the end of the list is reached; works on unsorted data.
Repeated passes comparing neighbouring items and swapping them if out of order, until a pass makes no swaps.
Found at position k: k comparisons. Not in a list of n items: n comparisons.
At most n − 1 passes for n items; each pass puts the next largest item in its final place.
Set FALSE at the start of each pass, TRUE on a swap; still FALSE at the end means sorted, so stop.
Temp ← List[i]; List[i] ← List[i + 1]; List[i + 1] ← Temp.
Found ← FALSE; WHILE Found = FALSE AND Index <= n … sets Found ← TRUE on a match, else Index ← Index + 1.
Swap when List[i] > List[i + 1] for ascending; use < for descending. Strings sort alphabetically.
FOR Index ← 1 TO Last − 1, because each comparison also reads List[Index + 1].
